What's the takeaway? What should a builder do differently after today?

Two things. First — study the Glasswing disclosure carefully. Ten thousand bugs in a small partner set means every codebase has vulnerabilities you haven't found yet. AI-assisted security auditing is no longer optional infrastructure for serious projects.

The keiretsu thesis is real. If you're building anything serious, you need to own more of your stack than you think. The companies that survive platform shifts aren't the most focused — they're the ones that controlled enough layers to not be evicted from any single one.
Build more. Own more. And maybe audit your repos for files named importantAWStokens.
